articles.headline: How Iowa ended up with Van Hayden, college football's most unique cover band
articles.description: A group of Hawkeyes fans decided to learn Van Halen covers as a bit. Now they're the life of the party on game days.

images.name: Van Hayden - LEDE [1296x729]
images.caption: Monday through Friday, they fill prescriptions, write code, consult on health plans and restore historic homes. On Saturdays in Iowa City, they put on white pants, aviators and fake mustaches, climb into a retired ambulance and become Van Hayden.

images.name: 01 - Van Hayden Inline [2000x4043]
images.caption: Legendary Iowa coach Hayden Fry wanted the Hawkeyes to look good, and rock gods Van Halen packed arenas. The spirit of both '80s icons combine at Van Hayden's tailgate concerts.
images.credit: AP Photo/Reed Saxon, Mary Beth Koeth for ESPN, Fin Costello/Redferns

images.name: 02 - Van Hayden Inline [8031x5357]
images.caption: Andy Olson (Eddie Van Hayden), Jake Olson (Alex Van Hayden), 15-year-old Masen Funk (The Pasadena Kid) and Brent Buresh (Michael Van Hayden) lay down the grooves while Robby Marvin, front, gets the crowd going as Hayden Lee Roth.

images.name: 03 - Van Hayden Inline [2000x2674]
images.caption: Four-year-old Sofia Thieleane Raecker, with her grandfather Steve Raecker, planned ahead and brought her own guitar to the family tailgate at the Dental Science Building in anticipation of Van Hayden's appearance before the Ohio State game.

images.name: 04 - Van Hayden Inline [2000x4043]
images.caption: Van Hayden makes several tailgate stops a day in multiple lots, including for a gathering of Fry's former players (top). The band has its own devotees, including Brandon Snell (middle), who wore a Van Hayden shirt and Zubaz pants to see them play.

article.story: Missouri State (1-3) at Western Kentucky (1-4), Oct. 8 at 7 p.m. EDT. Opening Line: Western Kentucky by 1.5. Against the spread: Western Kentucky 2-3, Missouri State 2-2. How to watch: CBS Sports Network Key stats Western Kentucky Offense Overall: 346.2 yards per game (108th in FBS) Passing: 233 yards per game (69th) Rushing: 113.2 yards per game (122nd) Scoring: 19.8 points per game (115th) Western Kentucky Defense Overall: 421.6 yards per game (123rd in FBS) Passing: 204 yards per game (64th) Rushing: 217.6 yards per game (132nd) Scoring: 39.6 points per game (135th) Missouri State Offense Overall: 349 yards per game (104th in FBS) Passing: 210.3 yards per game (89th) Rushing: 138.8 yards per game (96th) Scoring: 24 points per game (98th) Missouri State Defense Overall: 446 yards per game (132nd in FBS) Passing: 258.8 yards per game (120th) Rushing: 187.3 yards per game (120th) Scoring: 32 points per game (122nd) Missouri State is 123rd in defensive third down percentage, allowing opponents to convert on 46.2% of third downs. Western Kentucky is 126th in the FBS with a -5 turnover margin, compared to Missouri State's 58th-ranked +1 margin. Missouri State is 118th in the FBS averaging 72 penalty yards per game, compared to Western Kentucky's 14th-ranked 39.6 per-game average. Missouri State ranks 120th in FBS in red zone offense, scoring on 75% of trips. Missouri State is 135th in the FBS with an average time of possession of 25:55, compared to Western Kentucky's 83rd-ranked average of 29:33. Team leaders Western Kentucky Passing: Rodney Tisdale Jr., 857 yards, 4 TDs, 2 INTs, 66.7 completion percentage Rushing: Ajay Allen, 202 yards on 59 carries, 2 TDs Receiving: Jonathan Stafford Jr., 266 yards on 30 catches, 0 TDs Missouri State Passing: Skyler Locklear, 699 yards, 4 TDs, 1 INT, 70.2 completion percentage Rushing: Jambres Dubar, 209 yards on 37 carries, 2 TDs Receiving: Isaiah Myers, 342 yards on 17 catches, 2 TDs Last game Western Kentucky was defeated by New Mexico State 34-13 on Oct. 1. Tisdale passed for 314 yards on 29-of-40 attempts (72.5%) with no touchdowns and one interception. Brock Glenn had 23 rushing yards on seven carries and one touchdown. Stafford had 10 receptions for 108 yards. Missouri State fell to SMU 34-24 on Sept. 26. Locklear led Missouri State with 102 yards on 15-of-19 passing (78.9%) for one touchdown and no interceptions. Dubar carried the ball seven times for 76 yards, adding one reception for three yards. Myers had five receptions for 46 yards and one touchdown. Next game Western Kentucky plays at Sam Houston on Oct. 14. Missouri State hosts Kennesaw State on Oct. 14.
